walkthrough: For normal incidence the grating equation is $d\sin\theta = n\lambda$, where $d$ is the slit spacing and $n$ is the order number.
The same diffraction angle $\theta$ with the same grating means $d\sin\theta$ is identical, so $n\lambda$ must be identical for the two overlapping spectra.
Set the second-order term equal to the third-order term: $2 \times 600\text{ nm} = 3 \times \lambda$.
Solve: $\lambda = 1200/3\text{ nm} = 400\text{ nm}$, with the same unit $\text{nm}$ on both sides. This is option B.
